recommendation: ADOPT the symmetric recording-time/content-based citation convention only after correcting the citation grammar/count and completing the promised mechanical projection. A sibling version change alone should not require a successor; own-lineage supersession, supersession of an occupancy consumed as specification, or a change in any relied-on cross-lineage fact should require one.
rationale: The central convention remains the better reading: the recorded D-282 and D-285 ROW-to-ROW tolerance precedents join the earlier directional precedents, and all ten currently disputed predecessor/successor pairs preserve registerRow and leftoverDesign while the extracted obligation assertions preserve presence and value. Claude's provenance path, five-ROW-plus-DR-G07 wording, D-270/D-271/D-274 classification, ROW-to-ROW precedent discussion, and C-D293 token now match the bytes. The round-3 claim that every amendment was applied nevertheless fails in two material places. First, the stated dotted-or-spaced semantic grammar produces 27 sites, not 26: the packaging row omits its spaced-form remeasurementClause citation, and neither the measurement-rule paragraph nor Decision clause 1 actually states the full widened grammar. Second, clause 2(b) gives exact comparisons for partitions, registerRow, and obligation flags but leaves owner, status-token, and non-stealing facts to the undefined phrase 'reads the same'; that is not a mechanical field/value projection. The convention should therefore be adopted with those corrections, not in the regenerated form unchanged.

That catch-all remains semantic judgment rather than the mechanical field/value projection requested in round 2.

Replace clause 2(b)'s 'reads the same' catch-all with exact source fields and equality rules for any asserted owner, status-token, routing, and non-stealing fact, and require a successor whenever any projected value changes.
